criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear goal, four numbered objectives/requirements, named users with distinct needs, and rationale grounded in bleaching evidence and cited literature. Objectives are traced back to user needs. Slight weakness: requirement values (10 m, weekly, 24 h) are asserted rather than derived from sources.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef, so that bleaching is detected within days
The satellite would be operated by the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS). Its customers are the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt chart with dated weeks, per-task descriptions, sequencing justified by mission logic, a risk/contingency table with triggers and responses, and a source table. Software choice (STK) justified against mission questions. Minor: STK Simulations bar runs into Week 10 despite text saying completion by Week 9.

evidence.quote: The order follows the mission: the imaging requirements (objectives 1 and 2) fix the orbit altitude and local time
Week 10 is float as well as editing time: no new design work is planned in it.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Hand calculations for a, T, orbits/day, SSO inclination, ground-track shift and swath are numerically correct and interpreted, exposing a genuine coverage shortfall that feeds the contingency plan. Inclination is stated without working, and the coverage conclusion is qualitative rather than quantified.

evidence.quote: the reef is up to about 250 km wide, so a 60 km swath needs at least five neighbouring passes
A first STK scenario with this orbit has been set up, and its period agrees with the hand calculation.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical structure, clear headings, readable prose, labelled figure and tables, consistent formatting, and in-text citations matching the reference list. Deductions: reference [6] (NOAA climate-change page) is cited for BoM sea-surface-temperature products, and [4] is a news article rather than the primary method source.

evidence.quote: Figure 1: Project Gantt chart, Weeks 2 to 10 (gold = completed, blue = planned, red lines = report deadlines).

technical_issues.issue: Sun-synchronous inclination of 97.8° is stated without the J2 nodal-precession working, so the key orbit assumption cannot be checked.
Coverage conclusion is qualitative; no explicit swath-count or revisit calculation (e.g. passes needed vs daylight passes per week) is shown to prove weekly coverage fails.
Requirement values (10 m GSD, weekly revisit, 24 h delivery) are asserted rather than derived from the cited sources or sensor trade.
Reference [6] is a NOAA climate-change page but is cited as the source of BoM sea-surface-temperature products; no BoM source is listed.
Gantt shows STK Simulations running through Week 10, contradicting the text that final design and simulation finish by end of Week 9.

overall: Strong, well-structured preliminary report: a well-argued Australian reef-monitoring mission with clear users, a justified STK-based plan with contingencies and sources, and correct preliminary orbit calculations that honestly expose a coverage shortfall. Main gaps are unshown inclination working, unquantified revisit analysis, and one mismatched citation.

feedback.summary: Your reef-monitoring mission is well argued and clearly structured. You name users and needs, justify an STK-based plan with contingencies and sources, and your orbit calculations correctly expose a coverage shortfall. To reach the top of the Accomplished band, show the inclination working, quantify the revisit shortfall, derive requirement values, and fix the [6] citation and Gantt Week 10 inconsistency.
next_steps: In Preliminary Progress, add the J2 nodal-precession calculation that yields the 97.8° sun-synchronous inclination, so the key orbit assumption can be checked.
Quantify the coverage shortfall: count required swaths/passes versus daylight passes per week to show explicitly why weekly revisit fails, rather than concluding qualitatively.

Reconcile the Gantt (Image 1) with the text: STK Simulations runs to Week 10 while the text says design and simulation finish by Week 9; also replace reference [6] with a BoM sea-surface-temperature source.

criteria.C1: You give a clear goal, four numbered objectives and named users (AIMS, GBRMPA) with distinct needs, grounded in bleaching evidence and cited literature. To secure full marks, derive the 10 m GSD, weekly revisit and 24 h delivery values from your sources or a sensor trade, rather than asserting them, and tie each requirement explicitly back to the user need it serves.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt (Figure 1) has dated weeks, per-task descriptions and mission-driven sequencing, plus a risk/contingency table with triggers and a source table; STK is justified against mission questions. For full marks, align the Gantt with your text: the STK Simulations bar runs to Week 10 although you state design and simulation finish by Week 9. Clarify whether Week 10 is float only.
criteria.C3: Your hand calculations for a, T, orbits/day, SSO inclination, ground-track shift and swath are numerically correct and interpreted, and they honestly expose a coverage shortfall that feeds your contingency plan. To reach full marks, show the J2 nodal-precession working behind the 97.8° inclination, and quantify the revisit failure by counting required swaths/passes against daylight passes per week rather than concluding qualitatively.
criteria.C4: The report is logically structured with clear headings, readable prose, labelled Figure 1 and Tables 2–3, consistent formatting, and in-text citations that match the reference list. For full marks, correct reference [6]: it is a NOAA climate-change page cited for BoM sea-surface-temperature products, so add the actual BoM source. Consider replacing news article [4] with the primary method source.
